answer: A vault burns one fixed-supply coin per numbered voting ticket; no identity grants or rebates. Validators mirror its public ledger, verify burn receipts and owner signatures, and count each ticket once toward a price signal. Conflicting owner-signed ballots logged before tally void that ticket without refund. A 100-coin budget buys at most 100 votes across 1, 10 or 100 keys, even with parallel clones or collusion. Extra names gain nothing. Corrupt validators accepting unbacked tickets break the bound; rich coalitions can dominate. This is not proof of unique humans.
